Touchline

28 leagues, from the Premier League to the Malaysia Super League, played out minute by minute, in a single match or a full cup

Pick two clubs and watch ninety minutes.

Pick a league for each side, then who plays at home and who travels. Mix leagues freely. Watch every pass, dribble and shot on the pitch, with commentary, tactics and expected goals alongside.

Home side
Away side

Home advantageThe home side gets a small edge in duels, passing and shooting. Turn it off to play on neutral ground.
TiebreakerIf it is level after 90 minutes, keep playing until one side wins.
Pre-match cutscene BetaA one-minute opening before kick-off: the buses, the tunnel, fans filling the stands and the concourse, the dressing room, the commentators, the tifo and the walk out. You can skip it at any time.
Post-match cutscene BetaA finish after the final whistle: the players leave the pitch, the stands empty, the crowd fills the halls and the club store, the commentators call the result, then the coaches pull out and the stadium is left behind from above. In a cup final it ends on the medals and the trophy.
Cutscene sound BetaGenerated music and a spoken commentary read by your browser's text-to-speech voices. Turn your sound on. Voices differ between browsers and devices.

Every player has his own passing, dribbling, finishing, defending, pace and strength. On each action the man on the ball chooses to pass, dribble, cross or shoot, and the result depends on him, the defender in front of him, the club's tactics (press, defensive line, tempo, directness, set pieces, counters), the expected goals of the chance, an optional small home advantage and how each side's day is going. Squads and coaches are as of 1 October 2026. Ratings, player traits and tactical profiles are my own estimates, and the tactics are my reading of each coach's style. Each player also starts with a fitness level, shown as the small bar beside his position. It drains with work rate, pressing and tempo, makes him slower and less sharp as it falls, raises his injury risk, and decides who the manager takes off. The same match number always replays the same way.
